chunks: Al-Bazzaz, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a mukatab (a slave who has contracted for his manumission) who died and left wealth: His wealth is divided among his heirs in proportion to what was freed from him, and what was not freed is accounted for his masters who contracted with him, and it is their wealth.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful, referring to Imam Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has entered into a contract to buy his freedom by paying a lump sum or installments.

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a freed slave divided between heirs and masters upon death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the distribution of a mukatab's estate by dividing it proportionally between his heirs and his masters, reflecting the dual status of the slave as both a dependent and a partial owner. This ruling, attributed to the practice of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (AS), underscores the principle that the portion of the manumission contract already paid becomes the mukatab's private property, while the unpaid balance remains the masters' claim. It highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the liquidation of debt against inheritance in the context of slavery.
